caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: DANDI:001436
attempts.paper_title: AxonDeepSeg: automatic axon and myelin segmentation from microscopy data using convolutional neural networks
attempts.entry_title: AxonDeepSeg TEM model on the mouse corpus callosum images (Zaimi et al. 2018)
attempts.summary: The TEM model's segmentation of mouse corpus callosum held up: with the released model, pixel-wise accuracy, axon and myelin Dice and axon detection matched Table 3 for every possible set of 3 test mice, so it does not matter which ones the paper held out. The SEM model's rat results also matched, on rat images from a separate AxonDeepSeg dataset assumed to be the paper's. The macaque accuracy could not be tested: public macaque images give 0.5729 to 0.7634 against the paper's 0.8438, and the paper does not say which image or masks it scored. The human test image and the spinal cord slice behind the Figure 7 morphometric maps are not in the data.
attempts.description: Tests the mouse TEM findings of Zaimi, Wabartha, Herman, Antonsanti, Perone and Cohen-Adad (2018) on dandiset 001436, which holds 158 TEM images of the splenium of 20 control and cuprizone mice with manual axon and myelin masks. It runs the paper's released TEM model on every image and compares pixel-wise accuracy, axon and myelin Dice, and axon detection sensitivity and precision with Table 3. The SEM, human and macaque images and the rat spinal cord slice of the other findings are not in the dandiset; the macaque images of the White Matter Microscopy Database and the SEM rat test images of the AxonDeepSeg SEM dataset are tested as data from elsewhere.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Zaimi et al. (2018) from dandiset 001436

outcomes.statement: Each mouse of the dandiset (sub-nyuMouseNN) is the mouse of the same number in the NYU component of the White Matter Microscopy Database, which files its micrographs in one folder per diet group and time point, so that each mouse can be labelled as control or cuprizone.
outcomes.source: Data availability (the White Matter Microscopy Database, https://osf.io/yp4qg/, doi:10.17605/OSF.IO/YP4QG); Methods, Dataset (mice from ref. 27, Jelescu et al. 2016)
outcomes.notes: All 20 dandiset mice are matched by number to exactly one group folder of the OSF deposit, and no group folder holds more than 3 dandiset mice (ctl_6wks holds 2, mice 7 and 9; mouse 17 of that group is not in the dandiset). Of 39 OSF micrographs compared (11 mice), 16 have a counterpart in the dandiset (thumbnail r 0.593 to 0.903), all images of the same mouse, from 8 mice (10, 13, 14, 15, 25, 26, 27, 28); the other 23 correlate at most 0.487 with any dandiset image. Mice 7, 9 and 11 were checked without a counterpart among their first four OSF micrographs. Nine mice (12, 29 to 36) have no full-size micrograph on OSF and are linked by number only. The link gives 8 control mice (7, 9, 25, 26, 27, 34, 35, 36) and 12 cuprizone mice.
deviations: The correlation threshold of 0.5 for a counterpart was set on development runs on mice 25 and 26, before the full run, and written into the criterion then (see the claims file).

outcomes.statement: The TEM model trained on mouse images segments the mouse test images with a mean three-class pixel-wise accuracy of 95% (0.9451 in Table 3, mean over 24 test images).
outcomes.source: Results, Segmentation, paragraph 1; Table 3, row TEM, Mice
outcomes.quote: The TEM model trained on mice microscopy achieved a pixel-wise accuracy of 95% on mice samples
outcomes.notes: Mean pixel-wise accuracy 0.9416 over all 158 images of the 20 mice (reading a) and 0.9349 over the 62 images of the 8 control mice (reading b), both inside 0.8506 to 1.0396; the 96 images of the 12 cuprizone mice give 0.9459. Per-mouse means range from 0.9202 to 0.9740 and single images from 0.8954 to 0.9884. Every one of the 1140 sets of 3 mice gives 0.9226 to 0.9683 (the 56 sets of 3 control mice 0.9252 to 0.9441), so the outcome holds for whichever 3 mice the paper tested. Both readings include the mice the model was trained on, so the match is weaker evidence than a test on held-out mice. If the dandiset's 20 mice are the paper's 20, the paper's training set held cuprizone tissue (12 of the 20 mice), which bears on reading (b) but not on the outcome. Without the contrast inversion the accuracy is 0.5027 (a) and 0.3934 (b). The dandiset's masks are the 2025 revision; with the delineation lines filled (0 to 0.58% of the pixels of an image changed, median 0.12%), a variant for the masks the paper scored against, the accuracy is 0.9427 (a) and 0.9366 (b).
deviations: The paper's network runs in TensorFlow 1 (tf.contrib), which cannot be installed with Python 3.13. The network of network_construction.py is rebuilt with TensorFlow 2 operations from the released checkpoint; on the four patches of the first image its output differs from the model's own saved graph (model.ckpt.meta, run with training_phase False) by less than 1e-04 (the value printed in the notebook changes slightly between runs, at the level of floating-point round-off), and the classes agree on every pixel.

Resampling and histogram equalisation use the settings of scikit-image 0.13 (rescale and resize with order 1, mode constant, no anti-aliasing; an exact integer histogram), the release current when the code was published (it required scikit-image >= 0.12.3), as the defaults of the installed 0.26 differ.

The pixel size is the dandiset's 0.00236 um (sidecar files), as the criterion says, not the 0.002 um of Table 1; at 0.002 um the images would be 457 pixels high after resampling, smaller than the model's 512-pixel patch, so the code could not run them.

The ground truth is the dandiset's 2025 masks, in which every fibre is separated from its neighbours by a 2-pixel line (CHANGES, version 0.04), not the masks the paper scored against, which are not in the dandiset. The axon class is the axon mask and the myelin class the myelin mask.

Neither test-set reading is the paper's set of 3 held-out mice, which is not recorded; the range over every set of 3 mice is shown. Mouse 25 has 6 images, the others 8; no mouse has more than 8, so the criterion's rule for more than 8 images does not apply.
The control mice of reading (b) are labelled through the OSF deposit (osf-group-labels-link), as the dandiset names no group.

outcomes.statement: On the mouse test images the TEM model reaches a mean axon Dice of 0.9493, a mean myelin Dice of 0.8552, a mean axon detection sensitivity of 0.9597 and a mean precision of 0.9647.
outcomes.inferred: Numbers from Table 3, row TEM, Mice; the text states only the accuracy. The legend says that for the mice, 24 samples of the same size were used and the values are means over all samples.
outcomes.notes: Reading (a), all 158 images; axon Dice 0.9500, myelin Dice 0.8489, sensitivity 0.9863, precision 0.9707. Reading (b), the 62 control images; 0.9543, 0.8571, 0.9878, 0.9819. All four are within tolerance under both readings, and over every set of 3 mice (axon Dice 0.9300 to 0.9651, myelin Dice 0.8175 to 0.8739, sensitivity 0.9722 to 0.9969, precision 0.9304 to 0.9949). Over all images, 7757 of 7868 ground-truth axons are detected, with 239 false positives. Without the inversion axon Dice is 0.0029. With the 2025 delineation lines filled in the ground truth the myelin Dice is 0.8521 (a) and 0.8611 (b); the other measures do not change.
deviations: Segmentation, ground truth and test-set readings as in table3-tem-mice-accuracy.

score_analysis of segmentation_scoring.py is reimplemented with the same rules (predicted objects of area above 2 pixels, their integer centroids kept as a set, a ground-truth object with at least one centroid is one true positive, centroids in no ground-truth object are false positives, values rounded to 3 decimals per image as the code does).

outcomes.statement: In both models and every test sample the myelin Dice is lower than the axon Dice, which the authors attribute to myelin having two boundaries (with the axon and with the background).
outcomes.quote: In both models and all test samples, computed myelin Dice was lower than axon Dice.
outcomes.notes: On the mouse images, myelin Dice is below axon Dice in the means of both readings (0.8489 against 0.9500; 0.8571 against 0.9543) and in every one of the 158 single images (difference 0.0655 to 0.1556), so the claim holds under readings (i) and (ii). On the 7 macaque images tested for table3-tem-macaque-accuracy it holds too, and on the two SEM rat test images (myelin Dice 0.8720 and 0.8309 against axon Dice 0.9282 and 0.9186, table3-sem-rat-accuracy), which the criterion does not count. The human SEM row cannot be tested. The statement's explanation (two boundaries) is not tested.
deviations: Tested on the mouse images only, as the criterion says.

outcomes.statement: Axon detection sensitivity is above 93% in every test set (Table 3 gives 0.9300 for the human sample, so there the bound is met only with rounding).
outcomes.quote: In all test sets, sensitivity was high (>93%, see Table 3 ), indicating good capability to detect true positive axons.
outcomes.notes: Mean sensitivity 0.9863 (reading a) and 0.9878 (reading b), above 0.93; the lowest per-mouse mean is 0.9682 and the lowest over every set of 3 mice 0.9722. Two of 158 single images are at or below 0.93 (lowest 0.898). The other test sets of the statement are not counted by the criterion; on the two SEM rat test images sensitivity is 0.964 and 0.979 (table3-sem-rat-accuracy), above 0.93, and on the macaque images (table3-tem-macaque-accuracy) 0.289 to 0.606, below it.
deviations: Tested on the mouse images only, as the criterion says.

outcomes.statement: The SEM model trained on rat spinal cord reaches a pixel-wise accuracy between 85% and 88% on the two rat test images (0.8510 and 0.8822 in Table 3).
outcomes.source: Results, Segmentation, paragraph 1; Table 3, rows SEM, Rat 1 and Rat 2
outcomes.quote: The SEM model trained on rat microscopy was able to achieve a pixel-wise accuracy between 85% and 88% on the rat test samples
outcomes.notes: Tested on the SEM dataset of AxonDeepSeg (data elsewhere, tag r20211130, doi:10.5281/zenodo.5498378). Its sub-rat6 sample-data15 (0.13 um, 1154 x 744 pixels, 150 x 97 um, 3% PFA and 3% GA) and sub-rat8 sample-V915 (0.07 um, 1541 x 1096 pixels, 108 x 77 um, 3% and 3%) have the pixel size, field of view and fixation of Table 1's Rat 1 and Rat 2 test images, and six of its other eight images match Table 1's training rows in all three. The pixel-wise accuracy is 0.8955 (Rat 1) and 0.8757 (Rat 2), within 0.7659 to 0.9361 and 0.7940 to 0.9704. Rat 1's 0.8955 is above the statement's "between 85% and 88%", though inside the criterion's tolerance. The rebuilt SEM network agrees with its saved graph (largest difference below 1e-04, the same class on every pixel of the 8 patches of Rat 1). Variants, nearest-neighbour resize back 0.8923 and 0.8937; the 2025 masks of Rat 1 (0.31% of pixels differ) 0.8940; the contrast inverted 0.3047 and 0.3220. The other measures match Table 3 closely too (table3-other-samples-dice-detection). The images are tied to the paper by Table 1 only; the paper's Data availability statement does not name this dataset, which was created in 2020. The outcome rests on the assumption that these two images are the paper's Rat 1 and Rat 2 test images; a question to the paper's authors (methods_unavailable finding) asks whether they are.
deviations: Data from the AxonDeepSeg SEM dataset on GitHub, not the dandiset (data elsewhere), identified as the paper's test images by the pixel size, field of view and fixation of Table 1.

Assumed that sub-rat6 sample-data15 and sub-rat8 sample-V915 are the paper's Rat 1 and Rat 2 test images. The paper does not name its SEM test images or deposit them; these two match Table 1's test rows in pixel size, field of view and fixation, and six of the dataset's other eight images match its training rows, which supports but does not prove the identification.
The masks are those of tag r20211130, unchanged since the first commit (2020-10-08); the masks the paper scored against in 2018 are not public. The 2025 masks of Rat 1 are a variant.

Segmentation as segment.py does for default_SEM_model_v1 (working pixel size 0.1 um for a 512 patch, generate_resolution; overlap 25; no contrast inversion, which segment.py applies only for default_TEM_model_v1), with the network rebuilt in TensorFlow 2 as for the TEM model. The grey channel is used for Rat 1, whose png has an alpha channel (255 everywhere).
outcomes.where: SEM dataset of AxonDeepSeg, https://github.com/axondeepseg/data_axondeepseg_sem at tag r20211130 (commit d7884f9ab6cd8f06cba4885e752988a7706f0ede, archived as doi:10.5281/zenodo.5498378), sub-rat6 sample-data15 (0.13 um, 150 x 97 um, Rat 1) and sub-rat8 sample-V915 (0.07 um, 108 x 77 um, Rat 2), matched to Table 1 by pixel size, field of view and fixation; set by the author of attempt zaimi-2018-01

outcomes.statement: On the human spinal cord SEM test image the rat-trained SEM model reaches a pixel-wise accuracy of 81% (0.8114), the lowest of all test samples, which the authors attribute to the human sample's different contrast, quality and noise.
outcomes.source: Results, Segmentation, paragraph 1; Table 3, row SEM, Human; Discussion, Performance metrics, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: while the pixel-wise accuracy on human test sample was 81%
outcomes.notes: Not in the dandiset. The human spinal cord images of the White Matter Microscopy Database (PolytechniqueMontreal/Human, Duval et al. 2018, one zip file) have a pixel size of 230 nm by their description file (printed in the notebook), not the 0.13 um of the 715 x 735 um2 test image of Table 1, and the AxonDeepSeg SEM dataset, which holds the rat test images, holds rat images only.

outcomes.statement: On the macaque corpus callosum TEM test image the mouse-trained TEM model reaches a pixel-wise accuracy of 84% (0.8438).
outcomes.source: Results, Segmentation, paragraph 1; Table 3, row TEM, Macaque
outcomes.quote: and a pixel-wise accuracy of 84% on macaque samples
outcomes.notes: Tested on the macaque images of ref. 7 in the White Matter Microscopy Database (data elsewhere), 8 samples of three 2300 x 3040 images, with one myelin and one axon mask per sample. The masks of 7 samples fit one of their images (grey-level contrast of myelin 57.9 to 108.0 against at most 15.2 shifted, and at most 5.7 for the other images); those of sample 4 fit none. The paper tested one image and does not say which. On the 7 matched images the pixel-wise accuracy is 0.5729 to 0.7634 (mean 0.6723); one reading (sample 3, 0.7634) is inside 0.7594 to 0.9282 and six are below it, so the readings disagree and no image has a better basis than another. The other measures are below Table 3 on every image (axon Dice 0.6268 to 0.8070 against 0.9069, myelin Dice 0.5032 to 0.6481 against 0.7519, sensitivity 0.289 to 0.606 against 0.9429, precision 0.349 to 0.691 against 0.8129). Without the inversion the accuracy is 0.1810 to 0.3540. The ground-truth myelin covers 0.316 to 0.489 of these images and the predicted myelin 0.142 to 0.223. Pooled over the 7 images, 0.146 of all pixels are ground-truth myelin predicted as background and 0.090 ground-truth myelin predicted as axon, 0.719 of all misclassified pixels, so the masks mark much more myelin than the model finds on both of its borders; 0.067 are ground-truth axon predicted as background. With a nearest-neighbour resize back the accuracy is 0.5797 to 0.7678, so the resize step does not explain the gap. The same TEM code, with the same contrast inversion and resize, reproduces the mouse rows of Table 3 (table3-tem-mice-accuracy, table3-tem-mice-dice-detection), so these masks or images may not be the ones the paper scored, but this is not shown; the deposit's description, wiki and folders hold no description of the macaque images. The verifier of round 1 would mark the claim not reproduced; the disagreement is recorded under verifications. Question for the paper's authors (recorded as a methods_unavailable finding) asks which macaque image and which masks formed the test sample, and at what pixel size it was segmented.
deviations: Data from the White Matter Microscopy Database, not the dandiset (data elsewhere).
The pixel size is Table 1's 0.009 um; the NIfTI headers give a voxel size of 2.0, which is not a pixel size. 2300 x 3040 pixels at 0.009 um is 20.7 x 27.4 um, the 27 x 21 um2 of Table 1.
Each sample's masks are paired with the image they fit by grey-level contrast, as the deposit does not say which image they belong to.
Ground truth axon where avf.nii is above 0 (values 0 and 1/255), myelin where myelin.nii is 1.
outcomes.where: White Matter Microscopy Database, OSF node yp4qg (doi:10.17605/OSF.IO/YP4QG), folder MontrealNeurologicalInstitute/histology/Macaque (data/sample1 to sample8, segmentation/sample1 to sample8), files dated 2017-03-06; set by the author of attempt zaimi-2018-01

outcomes.statement: For the SEM test images and the macaque TEM image the axon Dice, myelin Dice, sensitivity and precision are rat 1 0.9089, 0.8193, 0.9699, 0.8468; rat 2 0.9244, 0.8389, 0.9876, 0.7987; human 0.8089, 0.7629, 0.9300, 0.7306; macaque 0.9069, 0.7519, 0.9429, 0.8129.
outcomes.source: Table 3, rows Rat 1, Rat 2, Human and Macaque
outcomes.inferred: Numbers from Table 3 only; no sentence of the text states them.
outcomes.notes: The human SEM test image is not public (see table3-sem-human-accuracy), so 4 of the 16 values cannot be tested. The 8 rat values, measured on the SEM test images of the AxonDeepSeg SEM dataset (data elsewhere, see table3-sem-rat-accuracy), are all within tolerance (Rat 1 axon Dice 0.9282, myelin Dice 0.8720, sensitivity 0.964, precision 0.887; Rat 2 0.9186, 0.8309, 0.979, 0.801). The 4 macaque values were measured on the 7 matched macaque images of the White Matter Microscopy Database (see table3-tem-macaque-accuracy), and every one is below its tolerance on every image (axon Dice at most 0.8070 against a lower bound of 0.8162, myelin Dice at most 0.6481 against 0.6767, sensitivity at most 0.606 against 0.8486, precision at most 0.691 against 0.7316); those images and masks may not be the paper's.

outcomes.statement: The TEM model slightly underestimates the myelin sheaths of the macaque sample compared with its ground truth.
outcomes.quote: Note that myelin sheaths of the macaque TEM sample are slightly underestimated when compared to the ground truth segmentation.
outcomes.notes: On all 7 matched macaque images (data elsewhere) the predicted myelin area is below the ground truth's, so the criterion holds under every reading of which image was tested. The underestimate is not slight; the predicted myelin fraction is 0.352 to 0.512 of the ground truth's, against 0.788 to 1.266 (median 0.974) on the mouse images. With the other macaque measures far below Table 3 (table3-tem-macaque-accuracy), these may not be the masks the paper scored against, so the direction carries little weight. The criterion tests the direction only, while the statement says "slightly"; whether the criterion should bound the size is asked of a reader (questions/zaimi-2018.yaml). The outcome rests on the assumption that the masks of ref. 7 in the White Matter Microscopy Database are the paper's macaque ground truth; the direction holds on all 7 images, so it does not depend on which image was tested.
deviations: Data, pixel size and the pairing of masks with images as in table3-tem-macaque-accuracy.

Assumed that the masks of ref. 7 in the White Matter Microscopy Database are the ground truth the paper scored its macaque sample against. The paper's macaque sample and its labels come from ref. 7 ("More details can be found about the generation of labels for the macaque 7", Methods, Ground truth labelling), and its Data availability statement names this database; no other macaque masks are public. The paper does not say which masks it used, and the other macaque measures, far below Table 3 (table3-tem-macaque-accuracy), leave open that they differ. The question to the paper's authors (methods_unavailable finding) asks which masks were used.
outcomes.where: White Matter Microscopy Database, OSF node yp4qg (doi:10.17605/OSF.IO/YP4QG), folder MontrealNeurologicalInstitute/histology/Macaque, as for table3-tem-macaque-accuracy; set by the author of attempt zaimi-2018-01

outcomes.statement: Segmenting a full rat cervical spinal cord SEM slice took 5 hours on a Mac laptop (2.9 GHz).
outcomes.quote: Processing time was 5 hours in a Mac laptop (2.9 GHz).
outcomes.notes: The full rat spinal cord SEM slice is not in the dandiset. The White Matter Microscopy Database holds two SEM panoramas of an adult rat cervical spinal cord, PolytechniqueMontreal/RatSpinalCordNov2016 (0.095 um, dated 2016-11-17) and PolytechniqueMontreal/RatSpinalCord2017 (0.13 um, dated 2017-04-27, next to a map of axon equivalent diameter), but the paper gives no pixel size, date or deposit for its slice, so neither can be shown to be the slice of Figures 6 and 7. The time also depends on the machine, a 2.9 GHz Mac laptop that cannot be matched here.

outcomes.statement: In the corticospinal tract of the rat cervical spinal cord the segmentation gives small axon diameters (around 1 um), very high axon density (around 200,000 axons per mm2) and g-ratios around 0.6.
outcomes.notes: The full slice is not in the dandiset, and neither candidate panorama on OSF can be tied to the paper (see full-slice-processing-time); they were not run. The criterion also leaves open which 50 x 50 um2 cells form the tract, as the paper gives the tracts only as a schematic diagram, and the paper's morphometrics come from AxonSeg, a separate MATLAB package.

outcomes.statement: Larger axons are found close to the periphery of the rat spinal cord.
outcomes.quote: Larger axons are found close to the spinal cord periphery.
outcomes.notes: As fig7-corticospinal-tract; the paper also gives no measure of distance to the periphery.

outcomes.statement: The diameter map agrees with the literature in that the ventral spinothalamic tract has the largest axons and the spinocerebellar tracts are mostly large-diameter fibres (both stated with citations, as known anatomy the map is consistent with), and axons of the cuneate fasciculus are observed to be larger than those of the gracile fasciculus.
outcomes.quote: The ventral spinothalamic tract (#3 in tract reference of Fig. 7 ) contains the largest axons ... We also observe that axons in the cuneate fasciculus (#7 in tract reference) are larger than those found in the gracile fasciculus
outcomes.notes: As fig7-corticospinal-tract; the tract boundaries are open.

outcomes.statement: Across the rat spinal cord white matter the g-ratio ranges between 0.5 and 0.75, in agreement with other rat studies.
outcomes.quote: G-ratio ranges between 0.5 and 0.75, which is in agreement with other rat microstructure studies
outcomes.notes: As fig7-corticospinal-tract. The paper's white matter mask is not given either.

findings.statement: The dandiset does not say which mice are controls and which received cuprizone, though its description says it holds both groups; participants.tsv gives only the species. The groups, and the time points, are in the folder names of the NYU component of the White Matter Microscopy Database (OSF node adrcs), by mouse number; by these, the dandiset holds 8 control mice (7, 9, 25, 26, 27, 34, 35, 36) and 12 cuprizone mice.

Neither the dandiset nor the paper's code records which 3 of the 20 mice formed the paper's test set (Table 1, 8 x 3 test and 8 x 17 training mice), so the mouse results of Table 3 cannot be repeated on the held-out mice alone. Every set of 3 mice gives values within the claims' tolerances here.

The masks in the dandiset are the 2025 revision (CHANGES, version 0.04, "Modify the masks of 155 images to separate all fibers with a 2px delineation"); the masks the paper scored against in 2018 are not in the dandiset.

The paper gives the mouse pixel size as 0.002 um and the field of view as 6 x 9 um2; the sidecar files give 0.00236 um and the images are 2286 x 3762 pixels (5.39 x 8.88 um). The dandiset's README explains both. At 0.002 um the images would be too small for the released model's 512-pixel patches.

The archive's assets summary for version 0.250512.1625 gives 11 samples, where the dandiset holds 158 images (samples.tsv has 158 rows); sample ids (sample-0001 to sample-0011) are reused across mice, and the summary counts distinct ids.
21 of the 158 axonmyelin masks are grey plus alpha pngs (alpha 255 everywhere), the others grey; their grey channel agrees with the axon and myelin masks in every image.

The dandiset holds only the mouse TEM images of the paper. The SEM rat and human test images, the SEM training images, the macaque test image and the full rat spinal cord slice of Figures 6 and 7 are not in it. Of these, macaque TEM images of ref. 7 were found in the White Matter Microscopy Database, without a record of which the paper tested; the SEM rat test and training images in the AxonDeepSeg SEM dataset (GitHub, doi:10.5281/zenodo.5498378), which the paper does not name; and two candidate panoramas of a rat cervical spinal cord in the White Matter Microscopy Database, neither named as the paper's slice. The human SEM test image was not found.

Question for the paper's authors. Which macaque image formed the test sample of Table 3 (the White Matter Microscopy Database holds 8 samples of 3 images, with masks for one image per sample), which masks were its ground truth, and at what pixel size was it segmented? On the 7 image and mask pairs found, the accuracy is 0.573 to 0.763 against 0.8438 in Table 3.

Question for the paper's authors. Are sub-rat6 sample-data15 and sub-rat8 sample-V915 of the AxonDeepSeg SEM dataset (doi:10.5281/zenodo.5498378) the SEM test images Rat 1 and Rat 2 of Table 1, and are its masks at tag r20211130 the ground truth they were scored against? They match Table 1's test rows in pixel size, field of view and fixation, and give a pixel-wise accuracy of 0.8955 and 0.8757 against 0.8510 and 0.8822 in Table 3.
In the White Matter Microscopy Database macaque folder (outside the dandiset), the masks of sample 4 fit none of its three images, and the NIfTI headers give a voxel size of 2.0 with no pixel size.

The SEM test images of Rat 1 and Rat 2 and most of the SEM training images of Table 1 are public in the SEM dataset of AxonDeepSeg (https://github.com/axondeepseg/data_axondeepseg_sem, doi:10.5281/zenodo.5498378), identified by pixel size, field of view and fixation, though the paper's Data availability statement names only the White Matter Microscopy Database. The masks of 6 of its 10 images, Rat 1 among them, were changed in 2025 to separate touching fibres.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: The first executed notebook with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper's full text. The verifier queried only the DANDI API, not OSF, and tested the helpers on synthetic inputs (score_analysis, pw_dice, pixel_accuracy, im2patches_overlap and patches2im_overlap, and the resize back of a class map).

disagreements.reason: Only 1 of 7 matched images is within 0.7594 to 0.9282 (sample3 at 0.7634, just inside); the mean is 0.6723, and every reading misses the other macaque metrics by far, e.g. sensitivity 0.29 to 0.61 against 0.9429. It is uncertain whether the OSF masks are the paper's ground truth. With predicted myelin about 0.45 of the ground truth, myelin Dice cannot exceed about 0.62, yet the paper reports 0.7519; so either these masks or this image are not what the paper used, or the pipeline differs. The not reproduced outcome rests on taking the OSF masks as the paper's ground truth, which the notebook does not show. Resizing the class map back bilinearly and casting to uint8 shifts boundaries toward myelin, which could matter for the macaque. Asked for any OSF description of which image and masks the paper used, and a per-class confusion matrix or overlay.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 2. The full executed notebook of the first revision, with its conclusions and summary, the helper module, the claims file, the attempt record and the README, with the paper's full text. The verifier checked each outcome, each assumption, every sentence of the conclusions and the summary against the outputs, and the status of its round-1 points.

entries.name: zaimi-2018
entries.title: AxonDeepSeg TEM model on the mouse corpus callosum images (Zaimi et al. 2018)
entries.description: Tests the mouse TEM findings of Zaimi, Wabartha, Herman, Antonsanti, Perone and Cohen-Adad (2018) on dandiset 001436, which holds 158 TEM images of the splenium of 20 control and cuprizone mice with manual axon and myelin masks. It runs the paper's released TEM model on every image and compares pixel-wise accuracy, axon and myelin Dice, and axon detection sensitivity and precision with Table 3. The SEM, human and macaque images and the rat spinal cord slice of the other findings are not in the dandiset; the macaque images of the White Matter Microscopy Database and the SEM rat test images of the AxonDeepSeg SEM dataset are tested as data from elsewhere.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Zaimi et al. (2018) from dandiset 001436
